content: 1. Inform your healthcare provider about all prescription and over-the-counter (OTC) medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and other supplements you are currently using. This information is crucial to avoid potential interactions with dexlansoprazole. Refer to the Interactions section for further details. 2. Do not take dexlansoprazole unless it has been specifically prescribed to you by a healthcare provider. Always follow the prescribed dosage and instructions. 3. Do not share dexlansoprazole with others, even if they have similar symptoms or conditions. This medication may cause harm to others if not prescribed for them. 4. Keep dexlansoprazole out of the reach of children to prevent accidental ingestion. 5. Do not chew, cut, or crush dexlansoprazole capsules. They should be swallowed whole. If you have difficulty swallowing the capsule, you may open it and sprinkle the contents onto one tablespoon of applesauce. Swallow the applesauce immediately without chewing, and do not mix the contents with any other food. 6. Dexlansoprazole can be taken with or without food. If administered through a nasogastric (NG) tube, follow the specific instructions provided by your healthcare provider. 7. Dexlansoprazole is not intended for immediate relief of heartburn. It may take 1 to 4 days for the medication to achieve its full effect. 8. Children under the age of 2 may be at a higher risk of experiencing certain side effects from dexlansoprazole. Consult your healthcare provider to discuss the risks if your child is under 2 years old. 9. Before starting dexlansoprazole, inform your healthcare provider about all your current and past health conditions. Specifically, mention if you have low blood potassium (hypokalemia), low blood magnesium (hypomagnesemia), low blood calcium (hypocalcemia), low blood sodium (hyponatremia), or liver problems. 10. Dexlansoprazole may interact with other medications and supplements. Always inform your healthcare provider about any prescription or OTC medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, or supplements you are taking. This will help them determine if dexlansoprazole is safe and appropriate for you. 11. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, inform your healthcare provider. It is not known whether dexlansoprazole can affect pregnancy or harm an unborn baby. 12. If you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed, inform your healthcare provider. It is not known whether dexlansoprazole passes into breast milk. 13. There are no known interactions between dexlansoprazole and specific foods or drinks. However, it is unclear whether alcohol consumption affects the medication. Consult your healthcare provider for guidance. 14. Dexlansoprazole may interact with certain medications, including methotrexate, digoxin, warfarin, tacrolimus, antiretroviral medications (e.g., rilpivirine, nelfinavir, saquinavir), St. John’s Wort, and rifampin. Inform your healthcare provider if you are taking any of these medications or others that may alter blood levels of dexlansoprazole or vice versa. 15. If you or someone else has taken too much dexlansoprazole, seek immediate medical attention, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. 16. If you miss a dose of dexlansoprazole, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. 17. Dexlansoprazole is used to treat heartburn and conditions caused by excessive stomach acid, such as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) and erosive esophagitis (EE). It may also be prescribed for other conditions as determined by your healthcare provider. 18. Dexlansoprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. 19. Dexlansoprazole is available as delayed-release oral capsules in 30 mg and 60 mg dosages. It is marketed under brand names such as Dexilant and Kapidex, as well as in generic forms. 20. Store dexlansoprazole at room temperature, between 68°F to 77°F (20°C to 25°C). It can be exposed to temperatures between 59°F to 86°F (15°C to 30°C) for short periods, such as during transportation. 21. Common side effects of dexlansoprazole include diarrhea, stomach pain, nausea, cold symptoms, vomiting, gas, headache (in children aged 12 to 17), and sore throat (in children aged 12 to 17). Contact your healthcare provider if these side effects bother you. 22. Serious side effects of dexlansoprazole include kidney problems (e.g., acute tubulointerstitial nephritis), antibiotic-associated diarrhea (e.g., Clostridioides difficile infection), severe skin reactions (e.g., Stevens-Johnson Syndrome or Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis), Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS), lupus, vitamin B-12 deficiency, hypomagnesemia, bone loss, and fractures. Seek immediate medical attention if you experience symptoms of these conditions. 23. People allergic to dexlansoprazole, Dexilant, Kapidex, proton pump inhibitors, or any ingredients in the product should not use dexlansoprazole. Consult your pharmacist for a complete list of ingredients. 24. Dexlansoprazole should not be taken with certain other medications. Always inform your healthcare provider about all medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are using to avoid potential interactions.
